title: skill-evolution-playbook
summary: Practical design choices for evolving agent skills from execution traces: when one trajectory should update a skill, how conflicting lessons are handled, how negative evidence is preserved, how large an edit should be, and when skills should split or merge. Drawn from Trace2Skill and SkillOpt. Use when designing or operating a skill evolution pipeline.

skill_metadata.name: skill-evolution-playbook

Drawn from Trace2Skill and SkillOpt. Use when designing or operating a skill evolution pipeline.

applicability.scope: Design choices for evolving agent skills from execution traces, drawn from Trace2Skill and SkillOpt: when a trajectory should update a skill, how conflicting lessons are handled, how negative evidence is preserved, how large an edit should be and when skills split or merge; for designing or operating a skill evolution pipeline
applicability.prerequisites: A final-test partition kept outside edit selection and the incumbent skill retained for rollback; changing a skill's scope first needs explicit review of its identity and consumers
applicability.input_contract: Execution trajectories or trace IDs with the diagnosed causal failure and the successful behavior an amendment must preserve; the incumbent skill and its revision lineage; held-out evaluation results for candidate edits
applicability.produced_artifact: A scoped case or amendment proposal, or a consolidated candidate edit, with rejection records and the versioned revision lineage; a candidate for independently evaluated acceptance, not a replacement decision or an efficacy claim
failure_modes: An anecdote, or agreement among analysts, is taken as efficacy
Consolidation output is treated as a replacement decision instead of a candidate awaiting independent acceptance
A tie or uncertain result is reported as improvement
A conflict is resolved by voting for whichever outcome appeared more often in the pool
A rejection is applied to every future use of an idea instead of the comparison it constrains
Paper-specific section counts or length budgets are used as universal defaults, or a skill is split on length alone
A stronger task solver is assumed to be a stronger improver, or replay rankings and private inner scores are read as outer generalization
applicability.refusal_point: Records a conflict that conditioning cannot resolve, where the same context produces different outcomes across runs, as INCONCLUSIVE and flags it for human review instead of choosing a lesson; claims no universal minimum trace count, paper-to-code equivalence or local efficacy

recommendations: Condition a conflicting lesson on its context (when X, do A; when Y, avoid A) before choosing one side.
Store each rejection record with its evaluation evidence, outside the deployed task procedure, and give it a retirement condition.
Bound the target passage and intended behavior before editing, inspect the actual diff and preserve rollback state.
Prefer an amendment when the existing skill owns the workflow; create a new candidate only for a genuinely distinct capability.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.
